# Producing a prototype

A `ui: true` ticket needs something a reviewer can look at before the code
exists. In the `maintain` profile that something is
`accord/assets/<id>/prototype.html`, and it is derived from what the project
already looks like — not from a fresh idea of what it could look like.

## 1. Find the styles the project already has

Before writing any markup, find where the look of this project is defined.
Look for, in roughly this order:

- the path named under `design.tokens` in `accord/config.yml`, if one is set;
- a stylesheet or variables file the application loads on every page;
- a utility-class configuration, if the project styles that way;
- a components or design-system folder.

Read what you find. You are looking for the names the project uses for its
colours, spacing, radii, and type — those names are what the prototype spends,
and inventing new ones is a redesign the ticket did not ask for.

If you find nothing, say so in the ticket's `## Open questions` and keep
going: a prototype built from nothing has to record what it was built from
instead.

## 2. Start from a single HTML file

One HTML file: a comment block at the top, an empty body. The comment block
names the ticket, a `Derived from:` line for what step 1 found, and the owner.
Build the page underneath it. One file, no build step, no assets directory —
a reviewer opens it in a browser and it works.

## 3. Put it where the gate looks

`accord/assets/<id>/prototype.html`, with `<id>` the ticket id. That folder is
this stage's own; nothing else writes into it.

## 4. Run `accord lint` and fix what it reports

Do not work from memory of the rules — run it, read the reasons, and fix what
it names.

A finding you disagree with is a question, not a licence: write it into the
ticket's `## Open questions` and stop, rather than working around the rule.

## 5. Re-run the gate

`accord gate ready <id>` is the only thing that says whether the ticket now
has what it was missing.
